terms.grammar: interjection, set off by commas inside a question
evidence: Ter. Eun. 4.7.10: Quī, malum, aliī? (Lewis & Short), s.v. alius
Ter. Heaut. 4.3.38: Quid, malum, mē aetātem cēnsēs velle id adsimulārier (Lewis & Short), s.v. aetās
terms.comment: “Mischief!”: the noun malum thrown into a question in annoyance, as English “the heck”. For “where on earth?”, ubi gentium (see where).

sources: Lewis & Short: malum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 100, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
